subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Hempcrete: Building with Plants
description: A quick win: understand Hempcrete: Building with Plants.

hook.text: Hempcrete is a building material made from hemp fibers and lime. It's carbon-negative.

buildup.text: Hemp plants absorb CO2 while growing. Mixed with lime, the material continues absorbing CO2 for decades.

discovery.text: Hempcrete insulates, regulates humidity, and resists mold. One material does three jobs.

twist.text: It's not structural — you can't build a skyscraper from it. It fills frames made of timber or steel.

climax.text: France has over 1,000 hempcrete buildings. Regulations are loosening worldwide as data proves its performance.

punchline.text: A building material that eats carbon dioxide.

quiz.question: Why is hempcrete considered carbon-negative?
options: It is manufactured using only solar-powered equipment
Hemp absorbs CO2 while growing and the material continues absorbing it
It replaces steel, which has higher carbon emissions
